how: Recruitment asks kindred participants for help and directs them to the coordinating room and maintenance task.
The early organiser credits a member with beginning the separate flag alone before inviting others to concentrate there.
One passage connects the attributed lone start to an invitation to concentrate effort on that flag.
A participant judges automation doubtful with fewer than twenty runners.

statement: translating for anyone who wants to help
how: Translation offers enable ordinary volunteers to participate without requiring an interroom envoy or border negotiation.
Offering translation makes the invitation usable by non-Spanish speakers, although uptake through that offer remains unmeasured.
Participants propose direction, width, equal stripes and a different alphabet while deciding the shared mark.
A participant reports four pixels already placed within the flag-design thread.
Explicit stripe-height instructions standardise the next placements without establishing the content of unseen linked templates.
A proposed advance receives a bare commitment to begin work.
The explicit proposal and immediate commitment support a local acceptance pair without establishing obligations or silent uptake among every reader.
This case occupies the acknowledged decided-order minority because uncertain helpers receive a maintenance role while others advance, without testing the population prevalence claim.
Script proposals and offers establish deliberation only, so machine placement must remain unresolved rather than inferred from discussion or a neighbour's bot.
Sharing a tool, questioning sufficient runners and requesting guidance form a decision stage that need not culminate in demonstrated deployment.
Moving from upkeep to machine placements depends on enough runners and usable guidance, neither of which is established as secured here.
Helpers prioritise keeping the flag clean and sweeping away vandalism while others extend it.
A painter identifies his own removal as a mistake caused by not knowing the shared proposal.
Establish whether a painter knew the agreement before interpreting mistaken pixels as deliberate refusal.
The room makes restraint a drawing method by growing behind others and preserving their borders.
Correction, private contact, apology and welcome repair an agreement's practical implementation when a painter did not know it.
Organisers inform neighbours, await responses, relay requests and report agreed plans.
An organiser carries a neighbour's request back to the group and accepts an invitation to discuss the border.
A settled agreement guides restraint only when painters learn its permissions and limits.
Agreement reinforces a restraint norm already expressed early, so it cannot explain the origin of all neighbour-sparing conduct.
Border negotiation also responds to blocked growth and neighbours' automated protection, beyond erosion of the room's existing mark.
Permission to use a neighbour's logo space is conditional on preserving its black pixels.
A neighbour requests help moving and later contributes available pixels to finishing the room's work.
A donor's completed work releases spare pixels, providing an explicit condition for help beyond the recipient's upkeep needs.
Negotiation precedes help here, but neither an exchange price nor negotiation causing the donation is established, while donor completion is explicitly named.
A bilateral border-chat invitation and acceptance do not establish joining a coalition or an agreement for mutual defence.
Maintenance and a border discussion are visible, but coalition membership and the proposed transition into it remain unresolved.
Administrators distinguish the room's adopted flag project from members' separate pixel efforts without claiming control over every participant.
Administrative neutrality and a painter's apology for ignorance do not establish a dispute over who may bind the room.
The record shows negotiation and information gaps but cannot establish the proposed transition into disputed authority.
Redirecting people to an already-started alternative flag does not establish relocation after their own work was erased or overrun.

statement: redirecting effort to a separate existing project before losing one's own mark
how: An alternative flag offers a practical exit from the useless war without requiring destruction of the room's own work first.
Replanning after losing intended growth space differs from rebuilding or relocating an erased flag.
Capacity doubts and lost expansion space do not establish the model's specified transition from inability to hold a spot into relocation.
Republican symbolism and political belonging shape the shield discussion, without establishing a preexisting subreddit.
The canvas conflict is described, but these concepts do not establish an intercommunity quarrel predating the event.
Political symbolism and an attack allegation do not demonstrate a pre-canvas tie naming the rival in the same attack turn.
The creator explicitly describes founding the subreddit to coordinate the Place corner.
A venue created for canvas coordination does not require the model's evidenced flood and containment response in an established host.
Explaining and inviting work on the flag does not establish a local fake or takeover framing the room's calls as pranks.
Participants celebrate the result, credit its starter and thank helpful neighbours.
A participant records the project's development from lone placing to collective work in a retrospective account.
Participants propose keeping the subreddit for political discussion, endorse continuation and point to a successor canvas.
Celebration and retrospective recording share one account, so the concepts do not establish celebration causing a separate preservation step.
The creator describes Place as an occasion for a desired lasting group, without establishing that a saved record caused the continuation proposal.
Perfection claims and an attack allegation do not show a dispute over cleaning a shared copy or preserving a particular historical version.
Member-level fighting, takeover reports and an outsider's allegation must not be promoted into an official campaign by an administration declaring neutrality.
The organiser explains the separate project as a response to existing war, preventing recruitment from automatically being treated as that war's cause.
The coded next-step call and retaliation warning establish reasoned restraint, but the cited call fragment alone cannot establish the full attack premise.
A peace proposal answering attack problems receives redirection advice and a participant's report of improvement rather than independently verified cessation.
The victory claim identifies no defeated rival, so it does not establish a continuing interroom contest in talk.
An attack allegation and an unnamed victory claim cannot establish attacks causing later rivalry talk.
A report of four placed pixels does not identify which invitation brought the painter or establish the proposed causal connection.
Early protection instructions establish upkeep but leave the initial build-to-defence causal sequence unresolved.
Completion celebration is clear, but these concepts do not establish reporting progress as the cause of collective celebration.
Design proposals, instructions and approval do not establish posting a template as the act that settled the disagreement.
